questions.q: What was the Rat doing when the Mole asked him a favour?
choices: Sitting on the bank, singing a song he made up about ducks
Rowing his blue-and-white boat up the river toward Toad Hall
Fishing with the Otter from the end of the little jetty
Cooking a big breakfast of eggs and bacon by the fire
questions.evidence: made up a song about them

questions.q: What favour did the Mole ask of the Rat?
choices: To take him to call on Mr. Toad
To teach him how to write poetry
To show him the way into the Wild Wood
To lend him the boat for the day
questions.evidence: won't you take me to call on Mr. Toad?

questions.q: How did the Rat describe Toad on the way to Toad Hall?
choices: Good-natured and affectionate, but boastful and conceited
Clever, quiet and very wise, but rather shy with strangers
Grumpy and unfriendly, and rude to every visitor
Brave and hard-working, but rather slow and dull
questions.evidence: it may be that he is both boastful and conceited

questions.q: When the Rat saw Toad's boat-house full of boats with none in the water, what did he figure out?
choices: Toad had grown tired of boating and taken up a new fad
Toad had gone away on a long trip to the Wide World
Toad was too sick with a cold to row on the river
Toad had sold every one of his boats to the Otter
questions.evidence: Boating is played out. He's tired of it, and done with it.

questions.q: Toad said his house was the finest on the river "or anywhere else." What does this show about Toad?
choices: He likes to boast and show off
He is very humble and modest
He wants to sell his house
He has never seen other houses
questions.evidence: Or anywhere else, for that matter,' he could not help adding.

questions.q: What was Toad's new passion that he showed his friends in the stable-yard?
choices: A canary-yellow gipsy caravan
A brand-new rowing boat with red oars
A shiny new motor-car with brass lamps
A racing horse with a silver saddle
questions.evidence: they saw a gipsy caravan, shining with newness, painted a canary-yellow

questions.q: How did the Rat feel at first about going on the caravan trip?
choices: He refused flatly and wanted to stay with his river
He was thrilled and began packing at once
He wanted to go but had too much work at home
He was afraid of the old grey horse and the road
questions.evidence: I'm not coming, and that's flat.

questions.q: Why did the Rat finally agree to go on the trip?
choices: He could not bear to disappoint the Mole and Toad
Toad paid him a large sum of money to come along
He had always wanted to see the Wide World for himself
The river had flooded and washed his home away
questions.evidence: He could not bear to disappoint his two friends

questions.q: Toad was "naturally a voluble animal." What does "voluble" mean?
choices: Talking a lot, quickly and easily
Very quiet and shy around others
Large, heavy and slow-moving
Easily frightened by loud noises

questions.q: How did the old grey horse feel about pulling the caravan?
choices: Annoyed, as he'd rather stay in his paddock
Proud to be chosen to pull such a fine caravan
Excited to see new places along the road
Happy because Toad fed him well on oats
questions.evidence: He frankly preferred the paddock, and took a deal of catching.

questions.q: On the first night, what did the Rat admit about his river?
choices: He didn't talk of it, but thought of it all the time
He never wanted to see it again after the long winter
He had already forgotten all about it in the excitement
He planned to sell his house there and travel for good

questions.q: Why did the Rat refuse the Mole's offer to run away home early the next morning?
choices: He felt he must stick by Toad, who was not safe alone
He was secretly enjoying the trip far too much to leave
He did not know the way home across the open common
He was afraid of walking home alone in the dark lanes
questions.evidence: It wouldn't be safe for him to be left to himself.

questions.q: What happened on the first morning while Toad was still asleep?
choices: The Rat and Mole did the chores and Mole fetched supplies
The old grey horse broke loose and ran away down the road
Toad got up early and cooked a fine breakfast for everyone
They all went swimming together in a pond near the camp
questions.evidence: the Mole trudged off to the nearest village, a long way off, for milk and eggs

questions.q: What wrecked the caravan on the high-road?
choices: A motor-car scared the horse, who backed the cart into a ditch
A wheel came off as they rattled down a steep hill near the town
A sudden storm blew it over while they slept on the common
Weasels crept up in the night and cut the horse loose
questions.evidence: he drove the cart backwards towards the deep ditch at the side of the road

questions.q: How did Toad react right after the motor-car wrecked his caravan?
choices: He sat in the road in a happy trance, murmuring 'Poop-poop!'
He shouted angrily at the driver and shook his fist at the car
He sat down and cried over his poor broken canary-yellow cart
He ran to help the Mole calm the frightened old horse

questions.q: The Rat said Toad was "possessed" by a new craze. What does "possessed" mean here?
choices: Completely taken over by one idea
Owning a great many things
Badly hurt in an accident
Very sleepy and slow
questions.evidence: He is now possessed. He has got a new craze

questions.q: How did the three friends finally get back home?
choices: They walked to the town and took a train back
They fixed the caravan and drove it home again
A farmer gave them a ride home in his hay wagon
They took turns riding the old horse all the way
questions.evidence: a slow train having landed them at a station not very far from Toad Hall

questions.q: What is the big turning point for Toad in this chapter?
choices: He gives up caravans and becomes crazy about motor-cars
He learns to work hard and always do his share of chores
He decides to stay home on the river and never travel
He makes friends with the old grey horse and buys him
questions.evidence: And he has ordered a large and very expensive motor-car.
